title: S&P 500 dip-buying levels: key support zones to watch
detail:
S&P 500 dip-buying levels: key support zones to watch
Investing.com
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:20 PM PST 3 min read
^GSPC
US500

Investing.com -- The S&P 500 (US500) is trading at 7,379.11, down 4.03% as of Nov 5, 2026, 3:48 PM EST. It dropped from an open of 7,682.76 and has lost 5.09% in a month. The intraday low is 7,356.37. The index is about 5.9% below its 7,844.52 high on Oct 6.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

This is a technical map, not a call to buy. The levels below are ones where past buyers have shown up.

Where buyers might look

Zone

	

Level

	

Why it matters




Intraday low

	

7,356

	

Today's low, the first test




Daily 200 SMA

	

7,323 (200 EMA at 7,342)

	

Long-term trend line, and the nearest major support




Prior support band

	

7,335–7,340

	

A support zone cited in a Sep 18 analysis (Read more)




June–July lows

	

~7,267–7,316

	

Prior bounce areas (Jun 10 low 7,257; Jul 29 low 7,314)




May lows

	

7,174–7,230

	

Deeper support, about 2.8% below the current price

The 7,323–7,356 area is the most important. The 200-day average, the cited support band and today's low all sit within about 0.5% of each other.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Momentum check

Oversold readings: The daily RSI is 34.3 and Williams %R is -94.9.

Still bearish: MACD is negative and the technical summary reads Strong Sell. +DI is 19.5 against -DI at 41.9, so sellers dominate.

Weak trend: ADX is only 17.5, so this is not yet an established downtrend.

High volatility: ATR is about 101 points, so the index can move 1.4% in a day. Stops placed too tight may be hit by noise.

Overhead resistance: The 20 EMA (7,648), 100 SMA (7,620) and 50 SMA (7,687) are all above the price.

Bull case vs bear case

Bulls: A November 4 analysis notes that November has historically been the S&P's strongest month, averaging gains of about 1.8–1.9% since 1950. It also says buying dips that hold key support has worked (Read more). Today's candle is a long red bar, which can precede a snap-back if support holds.

Bears: The index is below its 20, 50 and 100-day averages. Coverage from September flagged correction risk from rising yields and weak breadth (Read more). That article's technical levels are from September, so the current data above takes precedence. If the 200-day fails, the next stop is the May lows near 7,174.

Practical approach

Many investors scale in rather than pick one level. For example, they might buy in tranches around 7,356, 7,323 and about 7,230, and define a loss limit below 7,174. A break of the S&P 500 below the 7,323 area (the daily 200 SMA support) would weaken the dip-buying case. A rebound of the S&P 500 above 7,648 (the daily 20 EMA) would show buyers regaining control.

title: Update: Nasdaq Enters Correction Territory Amid Data Center Anxiety; Nvidia Tumbles Over 9%

^GSPC
SNDK

Stocks_Chart market equity trading wall street -Shutterstock

(Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

The Nasdaq Composite sank into correction territory Thursday as mounting regulatory concerns for US data centers sparked a sell-off in technology stocks.

The Nasdaq shed 5.5% to close at 24,315, its biggest percentage drop in a single day since April 4 last year. The tech-heavy index entered the correction territory, having fallen 12% from its record peak reached on Oct. 6.

A 10% stock pullback from recent highs is considered the minimum threshold for a market correction.

The S&P 500 slumped 4.4% to 7,353.73, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 3.4% to 51,523.06.

All sectors ended in the red, led by tech's 7.3% drop.

Shares of tech bellwether Nvidia (NVDA) tumbled 9.3%, the worst performer on the Dow. Semiconductor company Sandisk (SNDK) slid 22%, the steepest drop on the S&P 500. Other chipmakers also fell sharply, such as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Micron Technology (MU), and Marvell Technology (MRVL).

ING Bank sees potentially tighter data-center regulation following the Democratic Party's decisive victory in Tuesday's midterm elections.

"State-level policy will be more important to watch, as action is politically and practically easier at this level," ING said in a report Thursday. "The most likely approach is targeted regulation, much of which is already emerging. This includes data center-related taxes, reduced tax incentives, environmental standards, and requirements for developers to bear relevant cost increases."

Moratoriums on data center projects are unlikely to become mainstream, according to the brokerage.

"More broadly on AI, we expect the Democratic Party to increase scrutiny of technology companies, ... while utilizing the next two years to prepare an AI governance framework for 2028 and beyond," ING said.

Qualcomm (QCOM) plunged 9.5% as the chipmaker faces near-term margin headwinds from mounting data center investments amid component cost inflation, RBC Capital Markets said Thursday.

Applovin (APP) surged 31%, the best performer on the S&P 500, after the company posted stronger-than-expected third-quarter results.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil was up 3% at $90.73 a barrel in Thursday late-afternoon trade, while Brent climbed 4.1% to $98.50 a barrel, both rebounding after sharp declines in the previous session.

"A Democratic-controlled Congress could increase pressure to end the (US-Iran) conflict. However, no deal has been reached, and the two sides may still be far apart," Saxo Bank said in a report Thursday. "So far, oil has slumped more on hopes than concrete progress, leaving prices vulnerable to a rebound unless both Tehran and Washington signal a genuine willingness to compromise."

Treasury yields were lower, with the two-year rate down 12.3 basis points at 4.46% and the 10-year rate falling 5.7 basis points to 4.84%.

The Federal Reserve may need to continue raising interest rates to curb inflation, though at a gradual pace to minimize economic disruptions, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Thursday.

"I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Hammack said in remarks prepared for delivery at an event in Switzerland. "I prefer getting to that stance through more frequent smaller adjustments when possible, something which would be less disruptive to households, businesses, and financial markets."

Separately, Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said he expects further rate hikes, but is unsure of the scale and timing.

"Gradual makes sense if you think there's uncertainty in the world, and if you think that there's information you're going to get in the period," Barkin told CNBC. "And I think that's still a pace that makes sense to me."

Spot gold rose 1.1% to $4,103.38 per troy ounce, while silver edged up 0.3% to $52.45 per ounce.

title: Affirm Sinks 8% as Fintechs Slide Ahead of Affirm’s Earnings
detail:
Affirm Sinks 8% as Fintechs Slide Ahead of Affirm’s Earnings

Trading disclosure
Affirm Sinks 8% as Fintechs Slide Ahead of Affirm's Earnings ©@Przemek Klos from Przemek Klos via Canva, @formatoriginalphotos via Canva
Key Takeaways

Affirm shares fell 8% today with no company news, ahead of its fiscal first-quarter report.

Fintechs and chip stocks also slid as investors dumped riskier stocks after Democrats' midterm wins.

Going into the report, analysts expected Affirm's fiscal 2027 revenue to reach $5.49 billion.

Tonight's credit figures matter most: delinquencies at or under last year's 2.8% would make the drop look overdone.

Affirm (AFRM:NASDAQ) fell 8% today, ahead of its fiscal first-quarter results after the close.

The S&P 500 fell 4% and the Nasdaq-100 6% as the post-midterm rally faded, and retail-facing fintechs took some of the worst of it.

Nothing changed at Affirm today

Democrats won both chambers of Congress, and buy-now-pay-later lending has drawn lawmakers' scrutiny. I think tighter consumer-credit rules are the risk investors priced in today.

SoFi Technologies (SOFI:NASDAQ) fell 8%, just as hard, though its own credit is improving. On Oct. 27, it reported third-quarter adjusted net revenue up 44% to $1.4 billion and said its annualized personal loan charge-off rate fell 34 basis points from a year earlier, to 2.26%.

The chip selling ran deeper

Ciena (CIEN:NYSE) fell 15% with AI-networking stocks as investors weighed a slower data-center build-out after the election. Taiwan's chipmakers fell further: ASE Technology (ASX) dropped 21%, and United Microelectronics (UMC) fell 17% even though UMC said this morning that October revenue rose 18.33% from a year earlier.

TIKR tracks 36 analysts on Affirm. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Affirm, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Affirm's Analyst Ratings

What Affirm has to show tonight

Going into tonight, analysts expected Affirm's revenue to keep climbing, from $4.26 billion in fiscal 2026 (the year to June) to $6.85 billion in fiscal 2028.

Affirm (AFRM): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (years to June) (TIKR)

Nothing in today's selling gives analysts a reason to cut those estimates.

Management guided to quarterly GMV of $13.7-$14.0 billion and a GAAP operating margin of 11.5%-13.5%.

Credit is the bigger test. Upstart cut its outlook on Nov. 3, citing worse consumer credit and higher rates. Affirm's 30-day delinquency rate on monthly loans was 2.5% at June 30 and usually rises in the September quarter; a year ago, that quarter's rate was 2.8%.

GMV growth has to hold up too, after a miss on that measure sank Shopify, a key Affirm partner, 15%.

Before today, Affirm traded at about 19x forward earnings, below its 28x average since its forward P/E turned positive in September 2024, and lower still after today's drop.

Robinhood Sinks 10%, SoFi Down 8% as Bitcoin Slides and Fintech Stocks Sell Off ©Anna Nekrashevich from Pexels, Valerii Stoika from Valerii Stoika via Canva
Key Takeaways

Robinhood shares fell 10% today in a crypto-led selloff, pulling SoFi, Block and PayPal lower too.

Robinhood fell harder than PayPal and Block because most of its revenue still comes from customers' trading.

Analysts still expect Robinhood's normalized EPS to rise from $2.42 in 2026 to $4.37 in 2028.

The stock remains a bet on how much its customers want to trade.

Robinhood Markets (HOOD:NASDAQ) fell 10% today in a broad selloff that hit the market's riskiest stocks hardest, and SoFi Technologies (SOFI:NASDAQ) dropped 8% with it.

Bitcoin tumbled below $76,000. That gave back Wednesday's jump above $80,000, which came after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the midterms.

The big payments names held up better: PayPal Holdings (PYPL:NASDAQ) slipped 2%, and Block (XYZ:NYSE) fell 4%. With the S&P 500 down 4%, Robinhood fell more than twice as hard as the market.

Robinhood still lives on trades

In the third quarter, transaction revenue was about 61% of its $1.42 billion total, and crypto revenue fell 55% to $120 million.

Analysts still see growth

Analysts expect Robinhood's normalized EPS to barely grow this year, then jump to $3.39 in 2027 and $4.37 in 2028:

Robinhood Markets (HOOD): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

The stock has come a long way down from its October 2025 peak, though:

Robinhood Markets (HOOD): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Going into today, it traded at 27x forward earnings, compared with a three-year average of 36x. At today's price, it's about 24x.

SoFi got caught in the same net

On Oct. 27, SoFi reported that third-quarter adjusted net revenue rose 44% to $1.4 billion, and it raised its 2026 guidance. Lending brought in more than half of that revenue, so SoFi's results depend on credit far more than on bitcoin. I read today's drop as guilt by association.

Less trading, smaller drops

PayPal and Block make most of their money on payments and lending. Block's third-quarter gross profit rose 22% to $3.24 billion, and it raised its guidance on Nov. 3. PayPal also raised its full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance. At 10x forward earnings going into today, there wasn't much froth to sell.

Expect more days like this

With crypto revenue already shrinking, today's drop is fair. But at about 24x forward earnings, with analysts expecting EPS to grow about 80% from 2026 to 2028, I'd rather buy Robinhood on a day like this than after a rally.
